title: Katakana Reading Check
concept: Recall basic katakana and read beginner loanwords

questions.prompt: Match each katakana to its learner romaji.
questions.explanation: Katakana uses the same sounds as hiragana, so retrieve the known sound from the new shape.

questions.prompt: Match these t-row and n-row katakana to their learner romaji.
questions.explanation: Pay special attention to the stroke direction in ツ; it separates tsu from シ shi.

questions.prompt: Match these final-row katakana to their learner romaji.
questions.explanation: Use the full silhouette and stroke direction, especially for ン n and ソ so.

questions.prompt: Which pair is ordered shi, then tsu?
questions.explanation: シ has more horizontal short strokes and a rising long stroke; ツ has more vertical short strokes and a falling long stroke.

questions.prompt: Which character is the moraic n with a long stroke rising from lower left?
questions.explanation: ン rises from lower left; ソ begins higher and falls down toward the left.

questions.prompt: Which reading matches コーヒー?
questions.explanation: コ is ko, ー extends o, ヒ is hi, and the final ー extends i: ko-o-hi-i.

questions.prompt: Which katakana spelling reads hoteru, hotel?
questions.explanation: ホ ho + テ te + ル ru gives ホテル, hoteru.

questions.prompt: What does ー do in a katakana word?

options.label: It extends the preceding vowel sound.
It marks the topic of a sentence.

questions.explanation: The chōonpu ー is a long vowel mark; small ッ is the symbol that holds the next consonant.
